claims.text: Conventionally processed CoCrFeNi is a high-entropy-alloy matrix without secondary phases.
Uniformly incorporating WS2 nanosheets into CoCrFeNi before consolidation creates a self-lubricating composite.
WS2 nanosheets dispersed in CoCrFeNi will form a continuous lubricious tribofilm during sliding.
WS2 nanosheets align at the sliding interface.
At high temperatures, WS2 in the composite partially oxidizes to form tungsten oxides.
At lower temperatures, the layered low-shear interface of WS2 reduces friction.
At high temperatures, tribo-oxidized tungsten oxide phases maintain low friction.
At high temperatures, tribo-oxidized tungsten oxide phases reduce adhesive wear.
The combination of low-temperature WS2 lubrication and high-temperature tribo-oxidation extends self-lubricating behavior from room temperature to 800 °C.
WS2-modified CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi under identical sliding conditions throughout the room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
WS2-modified CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi under identical sliding conditions throughout the room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The proposed intervention is expected to remain effective in air from room temperature to 800 °C at constant load and sliding speed.
